  "title": "Sophocles, Hesiod, Euripides (18 tragedies), and Aeschylus",
  "tradition": "greek-latin-classics",
  "shelf_fit": "fits",
  "shelf_note": "A 14th-century Byzantine manuscript miscellany (the Laurentian codex) preserving canonical Greek tragic drama and Hesiod, fitting the classics tradition.",
  "rights_flag": null,
  "structure_note": "The 532 page records reflect a complete codex scan; 33 backsteps and 143 repeats in printed pagination reflect erratic manuscript foliation/cataloguing numbers rather than scan defects.",
  "on_sight_defect": true,
  "fit_to_show": "do_not_show",
  "showcase_pages": [],
  "reader_summary": "A reader encounters the 14th-century Laurentian manuscript of the Greek tragic poets and Hesiod. The OCR struggles severely with the Byzantine minuscule hand and compendia, mixing interlinear glosses into poetic verse and producing garbled text. The accompanying English translations either hallucinate coherent prose from corrupted Greek or drop substantial text entirely, such as a full column of Medea.",
  "book_verdict": "Unfit for scholarly presentation due to pervasive OCR degradation on Byzantine Greek minuscules, extensive translation hallucinations and omissions, and leaked metadata tags."
}

{
  "book_id": "69a5e60885fa13e734e42186",
  "slot": 6,
  "title": "Procli In Platonis Alcibiadem Commentarius (Barocci 140)",
  "tradition": "greek-latin-classics",
  "shelf_fit": "fits",
  "shelf_note": "Proclus' Neoplatonic commentary on Plato's First Alcibiades preserved in Bodleian MS Barocci 140 squarely fits the Greek and Latin classics tradition.",
  "rights_flag": null,
  "structure_note": "Metadata records 336 pages matching 336 digital scans and OCR pages, with 304 translated in metadata (334 in structure counts). The 162 recorded printed page numbers with 7 backsteps and 8 repeats reflect foliation skips, unnumbered flyleaves, or numbering inconsistencies typical of manuscript foliation rather than scan splices.",
  "on_sight_defect": true,
  "fit_to_show": "show_with_caveat",
  "showcase_pages": [],
  "reader_summary": "This volume presents Proclus' Neoplatonic commentary on Plato's First Alcibiades from Bodleian manuscript Barocci 140. While the digital scans represent the authentic manuscript leaf by leaf, the transcription struggles severely with 15th-century scribal ligatures and compendia, leaking synthetic XML markup into the display text. Consequently, the English translation regularly invents glosses for garbled non-words and reverses core Neoplatonic arguments, rendering it unsafe for scholarly use without constant collation against the manuscript images.",
  "book_verdict": "An important manuscript witness whose digital presentation is heavily degraded by scribal ligature misreadings, leaked prompt tags, and translation errors on key philosophical points."
}

{
  "book_id": "69a9768ee12635ded71c4e2f",

  "title": "Quaestiones de Primis Principiis",
  "tradition": "greek-latin-classics",
  "shelf_fit": "fits",
  "shelf_note": "Joseph Kopp's 1826 edition of Damascius's Neoplatonic philosophical treatise in ancient Greek with Latin commentary belongs squarely in greek-latin-classics.",
  "rights_flag": null,
  "structure_note": "424 page records matching the count field, with 420 OCR'd and 418 translated. 14 printed backsteps and 10 repeats reflect front matter pagination or minor typographical misreads rather than missing scan batches.",
  "on_sight_defect": true,
  "fit_to_show": "show_with_caveat",
  "showcase_pages": [
    98
  ],
  "reader_summary": "The work presented is Damascius's Neoplatonic treatise on first principles in Joseph Kopp's 1826 Greek edition with Latin preface and apparatus. The OCR correctly identifies the Greek text across pages, though synthetic XML-style tags leak into the reader transcription. The English translation reliably renders the philosophical arguments, but completely omits the critical apparatus notes and occasional transitional clauses.",
  "book_verdict": "A solid transcription of a complex Neoplatonic edition whose English translation is generally faithful to the philosophical prose, though degraded by dropped apparatus notes and leaked prompt metadata tags."
}

{
  "book_id": "69b52c953dd6d94230281474",
  "slot": 8,
  "title": "Vitruvii de architectura libri X",
  "tradition": "greek-latin-classics",
  "shelf_fit": "fits",
  "shelf_note": "A 13th-century Latin manuscript copy of Vitruvius' De architectura, appropriately catalogued under Greek and Latin classics.",
  "rights_flag": null,
  "structure_note": "Page counts are consistent across OCR and translation (116 pages total, 114 with OCR/translation). The high count of printed backsteps (18) and repeats (14) reflects irregular manuscript foliation or pagination numbers in marginalia rather than missing or duplicated folios.",
  "on_sight_defect": true,
  "fit_to_show": "do_not_show",
  "showcase_pages": [],
  "reader_summary": "This digital witness presents a 13th-century manuscript of Vitruvius' De architectura from the Laurentian Library, but the transcription regularly fumbles standard medieval abbreviations (turning Socrates into father-in-law and meridional into Indian). Pervasive system and XML metadata wrappers leak into the reader-facing transcription across multiple pages. The English translation inherits these transcription errors and drops substantial chunks of text, making it unreliable for scholarly or reference use.",
  "book_verdict": "A genuine medieval manuscript witness marred by leaky prompt/XML apparatus in the OCR and severe translation omissions and mistranslations driven by unresolved scribal abbreviations."
}
